entities.name: PMID:10754365
observations: Randomized four-condition scintigraphic crossover study in 12 patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus; compared placebo or 200 mg IV erythromycin during euglycemia (5–8.9 mmol/L) and induced hyperglycemia (16–19 mmol/L).

With erythromycin, hyperglycemia increased half-meal emptying time from 16.6 ± 6.0 to 24.9 ± 5.5 minutes and lag phase from 3.7 ± 2.5 to 7.8 ± 4.5 minutes; gastric retention at 60 and 100 minutes was higher, with reported p<0.001.
Conclusion: induced hyperglycemia attenuated but did not abolish erythromycin-induced acceleration of hypertonic liquid-phase gastric emptying; erythromycin remained prokinetic under hyperglycemia.

entities.name: Erythromycin
observations: At 200 mg IV, remained prokinetic during induced hyperglycemia but produced less acceleration of hypertonic liquid-phase gastric emptying than during euglycemia in type 1 diabetic patients.

entities.name: Hyperglycemia attenuates erythromycin effect
observations: In type 1 diabetic patients, induced hyperglycemia significantly slowed erythromycin-treated hypertonic liquid gastric emptying versus euglycemia: half-meal emptying time 24.9 ± 5.5 versus 16.6 ± 6.0 minutes; lag phase 7.8 ± 4.5 versus 3.7 ± 2.5 minutes; reported p<0.001.
This attenuation reduced but did not eliminate erythromycin's acceleration of gastric emptying.
